A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SLR framework and SLR-BENCH. All 20 pages of v3 and 26 pages of v5, including appendices, are readable, and retained methods, equations, figures and tables can be matched across relocations.

before.justification: v3 reports original LLM evaluations and Llama fine-tuning results on SLR-BENCH and downstream benchmarks in Tables 3–4.

after.justification: v5 retains original evaluations and adds transfer experiments, training comparisons, ablations and quantitative error analyses in Tables 7–16.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1 and the symbolic judge remain unchanged. Appendix F.3 adds a concrete GRPO training variant for DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-1.5B, extending the demonstrated training procedure beyond SFT. v3 already described generic RLVR support, so this is a limited training adaptation.

E1.justification: v5 adds SLR-Homes, comprising 500 house-classification tasks across five difficulty levels with different vocabulary and relational structure. It also evaluates CLUTRR kinship inference across six generalization and robustness variants. These substantially extend the represented evaluation domains beyond the retained train curriculum and downstream suite.

E2.justification: The evaluated comparator set expands substantially through GPT-5 and Qwen3 families, including reasoning-enabled and disabled variants, plus CoT comparisons and DeepSeek-R1-8B on CLUTRR. Random and reverse curriculum controls are also added. Earlier leaderboard models remain represented in the extended Table 16 despite omissions from the shortened main table.

E3.justification: New protocols include curriculum-order comparisons on levels 5–7 with matched data and token budgets, shuffled Qwen3 fine-tuning, and GRPO training stopped at level 7. v5 also introduces greedy-decoding CLUTRR evaluation and multi-completion Pass@1/4/8 and CoT testing. These are added experimental designs; the PDFs do not establish why existing leaderboard scores were revised.

E4.justification: Appendices E–G add synthesis-parameter comparisons, curriculum-order controls, cross-domain transfer tests, sampling/CoT sensitivity, and quantified error, shortcut and output-length analyses. These address questions largely untested in v3. Conversely, the o4-mini comparison in Table 9 and the relocated compute plot reuse earlier evidence.

E5.justification: Appendix F.4 newly states that Pass@k scores for k below 8 are averaged and discusses variability across sampled completions. This adds limited sampling and aggregation information, without establishing repeated training runs. Neither version reports training seeds, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests.

E6.justification: Existing reported values change: base/tuned Llama LRL moves from 3.6/8.8 to 3.8/8.7, and GPT-4.5 LRL from 7.6 to 7.3. New results include base/tuned Llama accuracy of 10.3%/42.3% on SLR-Homes and 25.5%/32.1% on CLUTRR, alongside Qwen3, GRPO and diagnostic results. Separate MMLU-CS/ML results disappear. Unexplained revisions to older scores do not establish same-setting performance improvements.

T1.justification: Section 3.1 refines the stated rule-length definition by excluding structural linking predicates, while Section 3 explicitly states the closed-world assumption. The existing FOL definitions and entailment-based reward equations are retained and relocated; no new theorem or proof is introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract and four principal contributions remain substantially unchanged. The conclusion narrows the claim that tuned Llama outperforms all conventional LLMs to most conventional LLMs, while the introduction broadens its training discussion from Llama specifically to SLR-tuned models.

C2.justification: v5 adds a systematic-rule-induction explanation for transfer, model-specific explanations of abstraction failures and shortcut behavior, and interpretations of reasoning-trace degeneration. It also qualifies semantic leakage guarantees and cross-model compute comparisons, and discusses GRPO reward collapse beyond level 7. These substantially extend v3's interpretation of accuracy, syntax and compute trends.

D1.justification: v5 adds mirror-sampling details, error-detection heuristics, and brief Qwen3, GRPO and CLUTRR setup information. Table 5 adds GPT-5/Qwen3 pricing while dropping many earlier pricing entries. The explicit two-epoch, approximately 17k-example training description disappears, without establishing an actual budget change. Core hyperparameters, code/data links and licensing remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v5 adds positioning against classic ILP datasets through Mutagenesis, cites De Raedt's learning-from-entailment framework, and adds the DeepSeekMath reference for GRPO. References to Fourrier's leaderboard and Mondorf and Plank's benchmark are removed. The broader research positioning remains intact.

P1.justification: Although the main section sequence remains, v5 substantially reorganizes existing appendix material into notation, benchmark details and training sections. It condenses the main reward exposition, adds task notation and a motivating example, and restructures the findings narrative around transfer, curriculum order and error modes.

P2.justification: v5 adds extensive dedicated displays for ablations, training variants, sampling results and failure analyses, plus an expanded leaderboard with organization symbols and a reasoning-enabled column. It also restructures the downstream table, moves the curriculum table and compute plot into the appendices, and changes caption placement. The original framework diagrams are largely retained.

improvement.justification: SLR-Homes and CLUTRR directly strengthen evidence for transfer beyond the train domain, while Qwen3 and GRPO experiments broaden validation beyond v3's single Llama SFT demonstration. Quantified failure analyses also make the framework's boundaries more assessable. These are substantial evidential gains, despite weaknesses: some parameter comparisons are confounded, curriculum-order scores are nearly tied without uncertainty estimates, and explicit epoch information is lost.
